source.text: 1. ἣν εἶδον, ἀδελφοί, τοιαύτη. 2. νηστεύσας πολλάκις καὶ δεηθείς τοῦ Κυρίου ἵνα μοι φανερώσῃ τὴν ἀποκάλυψιν ἣν μοι ἐπηγγείλατο δεῖξαι διὰ τῆς πρεσβυτέρας ἐκείνης, αὐτῇ τῇ νυκτὶ ὤφθη μοι ἡ πρεσβυτέρα καὶ εἶπέν μοι· Ἐπεὶ οὕτως ἐνδεὴς εἶ καὶ σπουδαῖος εἰς τὸ γνῶναι πάντα, ἐλθὲ εἰς τὸν ἀγρὸν ὅπου χρονίζεις, καὶ περὶ ὥραν πέμπτην ἐμφανισθήσομαί σοι καὶ δείξω σοι ἃ δεῖ σε ἰδεῖν. 3. ἠρώτησα αὐτὴν λέγων· Κυρία, εἰς ποῖον τόπον τοῦ ἀγροῦ; Ὅπου, φησίν, θέλεις. ἐξελεξάμην τόπον καλὸν ἀνακεχωρηκότα. πρὶν δὲ λαλῆσαι αὐτῇ καὶ εἰπεῖν τὸν τόπον, λέγει μοι· Ἥξω ἐκεῖ ὅπου θέλεις. 4. ἐγενόμην οὖν, ἀδελφοί, εἰς τὸν ἀγρόν, καὶ συνεψήφισα τὰς ὥρας, καὶ ἦλθον εἰς τὸν τόπον ὅπου διεταξάμην αὐτὴν ἐλθεῖν, καὶ βλέπω συμπέλιον κείμενον ἐλεφάντινον, καὶ ἐπὶ τοῦ συμπελίου ἔκειτο κεβριδάριον λινόῦν, καὶ ἐπάνω λεντίον ἐξηπλωμένον λινόῦν καρπάσιον. 5. ἰδὼν ταῦτα κείμενα καὶ μηδένα ὄντα ἐν τῷ τόπῳ ἔκθαμβος ἐγενόμην, καὶ ὡσεί τρόμος με ἔλαβεν, καὶ αἱ τρίχες μου ὀρθαί· καὶ ὡσεί φρίκη μοι προσῆλθεν, μόνου μου ὄντος. ἐν ἐμαυτῷ οὖν γενόμενος καὶ μνησθεὶς τῆς δόξης τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ λαβὼν θάρσος, θεὶς τὰ γόνατα ἐξωμολογούμην τῷ Κυρίῳ πάλιν τὰς ἁμαρτίας μου ὡς καὶ πρότερον. 6. ἡ δὲ ἦλθεν μετὰ νεανίσκων ἕξ, οὓς καὶ πρότερον ἑωράκειν, καὶ ἐπεστάθη μοι καὶ κατηκροᾶτο προσευχομένου μου καὶ ἐξομολογουμένου τῷ Κυρίῳ τὰς ἁμαρτίας μου. καὶ ἁψαμένη μου λέγει· Ἑρμᾶ, παῦσαι περὶ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν σου πάντα ἐρωτῶν· ἐρώτα καὶ περὶ δικαιοσύνης, ἵνα λάβῃς μέρος τι ἐξ αὐτῆς εἰς τὸν οἶκόν σου. 7. καὶ ἐξήγειρέ με τῆς χειρὸς καὶ ἄγει με πρὸς τὸ συμπέλιον, καὶ λέγει τοῖς νεανίσκοις· Ὑπάγετε καὶ οἰκοδομεῖτε. 8. καὶ μετὰ τὸ ἀναχωρῆσαι τοὺς νεανίσκους καὶ μόνων ἡμῶν γενομένων λέγει μοι· Κάθισον ὧδε. λέγω αὐτῇ· Κυρία, ἄφες τοὺς πρεσβυτέρους πρῶτον καθίσαι. Ὅ σοι λέγω, φησίν, κάθισον. 9. θέλοντος οὖν μου καθίσαι εἰς τὰ δεξιὰ μέρη οὐκ εἴασέν με, ἀλλ’ ἐνένευέ μοι τῇ χειρὶ ἵνα εἰς τὰ ἀριστερὰ μέρη καθίσω. διαλογιζομένου μου οὖν καὶ λυπουμένου ὅτι οὐκ εἴασέν με εἰς τὰ δεξιὰ μέρη καθίσαι, λέγει μοι· Λυπῇ, Ἑρμᾶ; ὁ εἰς τὰ δεξιὰ μέρη τόπος ἄλλων ἐστίν, τῶν ἤδη εὐαρεστηκότων τῷ θεῷ καὶ παθόντων εἵνεκα τοῦ ὀνόματος· σοὶ δὲ πολλὰ λείπει ἵνα μετ’ αὐτῶν καθίσῃς· ἀλλ’ ὡς ἐμμένεις τῇ ἁπλότητί σου, μενὸν, καὶ καθῇ μετ’ αὐτῶν, καὶ ὅσοι ἐὰν ἐργάσωνται τὰ ἐκείνων ἔργα καὶ ὑπενέγκωσιν ἃ καὶ ἐκεῖνοι ὑπήνεγκαν.

translation.text:
The vision I saw[1], brothers, was like this.

After fasting many times and pleading with the Lord to make known to me the revelation he had promised to show me through that aged woman, on that very night the aged woman appeared to me and said: “Since you are so needy and so eager to know everything, come to the field where you spend your time, and about the fifth hour I will appear to you and show you what you must see.”

I asked her, saying, “Lady, to what place in the field?” “Wherever you wish,” she says. I chose a good, secluded spot. But before I spoke to her and named the place, she says to me, “I will come there where you wish.”

So I went, brothers, into the field, and I counted the hours[2], and I came to the place where I had directed her to come; and I see an ivory seat set there, and upon the seat there lay a linen cushion, and on top a spread-out towel of fine linen.

Seeing these things set there and no one in the place, I was astonished, and a tremor, as it were, seized me, and my hair stood on end; and a shudder, as it were, came upon me, since I was alone. Then, coming to myself and remembering the glory of God, and taking courage, I knelt and again confessed my sins to the Lord, as before.

And she came with six young men—whom I had seen also before—and she stood near me and listened closely while I was praying and confessing my sins to the Lord. And touching me she says, “Hermas, stop asking everything about your sins; ask also about righteousness, so that you may receive some share of it for your household.”

And she raised me by the hand and leads me to the seat, and she says to the young men, “Go and build.”

And after the young men withdrew and we were alone, she says to me, “Sit here.” I say to her, “Lady, let the elders sit first.” “What I tell you,” she says, “sit.”

So when I wanted to sit on the right side, she did not permit me, but motioned to me with her hand that I should sit on the left side. So as I reasoned and was grieved that she had not allowed me to sit on the right side, she says to me, “Are you grieved, Hermas? The place on the right side belongs to others—those who have already pleased God and suffered for the sake of the Name; but you lack many things to sit with them. But as you remain in your simplicity, remain, and you will sit with them[c][b][a][8][7][6][5][4][3], as will all who do their works and bear what they also bore.”

footnotes.text: The fifth hour of the day is roughly mid-to-late morning (about 11 a.m.) in Roman reckoning.
The Greek address Kyria means “Lady,” a respectful form of address.
The term translated “seat” renders a rare Greek word (sympelion) for a piece of furniture; it may be a low bench or couch.
“Fine linen” translates karpasion (carbasus), a high-quality linen fabric.
“Righteousness” can also mean “justice,” depending on context.
“Household” translates oikos, which can mean a physical house or an extended household.
“Elders” (presbyteroi) may refer either to older men or to those holding an office of oversight in the community.
“For the sake of the Name” is an early Christian idiom for suffering on account of God’s/Jesus’ name (cf. Acts 5:41).
Or '“What I say to you—sit,” she says.'.
Or 'but for you, many things are lacking for you to sit with them.'.
Or 'stop asking all these things about your sins'.

lexical_decisions.rationale: ἣν refers back to ὅρασις (vision) from the heading; ἀδελφοί is the customary fraternal address in early Christian literature. We keep 'brothers' for historical texture; inclusive sense can be footnoted if needed.
Standard rendering for divine disclosure; preserves apocalyptic nuance without paraphrase.
πρεσβυτέρα here is the female figure already introduced in Visions 1–2; rendering as 'aged woman' preserves literal age connotation and avoids importing ecclesial office.
Κυρία as respectful address to a woman; 'Lady' maintains register and echoes the narrative's formal tone.
Here denotes where he usually lingers; 'spend your time' is idiomatic without losing sense.
We retain the ancient time reference; explanatory footnote gives modern equivalent.

alternatives: I kept count of the hours
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves concrete action of calculating the hours until the appointment.
Rare term likely indicating a low seat/bench; 'seat' is neutral. Footnote notes furniture uncertainty.
Material descriptor; straightforward.
Diminutive for a small pillow; 'cushion' conveys function without over-specifying size.
λεντίον is a towel/cloth (cf. John 13); specifying 'towel' keeps concrete domestic sense.
Refers to carbasus, fine linen; 'fine linen' communicates quality to modern readers.
Captures sudden, unsettling amazement; context includes fear markers.
Idiomatic English for the posture of prayer, preserving literal action.
Cultic/moral term for open confession; 'confessed' keeps the penitential register.
'Young men' reads naturally and is semantically precise.

alternatives: she came and stood by me
lexical_decisions.rationale: Locative nuance; 'near me' avoids a domineering connotation while keeping proximity.
Compound emphasizes attentive listening; 'closely' captures intensity.
Imperative with durative nuance; 'stop asking' is concise and clear.
Default Cartha rendering; moral quality in Hermas leans toward 'righteousness'. 'Justice' noted in footnote for semantic range.
οἶκος here likely includes household; 'share' preserves meros as portion.
Simple imperative; anticipates the tower imagery without explicating it.
Term can denote age or office; 'elders' preserves possible ecclesial nuance in Hermas.
Literal spatial terms are theologically charged (honor at right hand); keep literal.
Perfect participle indicates settled status; 'have pleased God' reads smoothly.

lexical_decisions.chosen: suffered for the sake of the Name
alternatives: suffered on account of the Name
lexical_decisions.rationale: Traditional early Christian idiom; capitalization of 'Name' reflects reverential usage.
Direct idiom for deficiency toward a standard.
Covenantal perseverance nuance; 'remain' is simple and accurate.
Hermas uses ἁπλότης as a moral quality opposed to double-mindedness; 'simplicity' preserves his category.
Avoids archaic phrasing while keeping the work/works lexical tie.
Carries the sense of enduring trials; 'bear' is concise and evocative.

theological_decisions.rationale: Maintains early Christian confessional register without over-specifying referent (God vs. the Lord Jesus). Hermas often uses 'the Lord' in a general theistic sense.
Hermas emphasizes personal and communal moral rectitude; 'righteousness' best captures this. 'Justice' is noted as an alternative in footnotes for readers aware of the broader semantic range.
Early Christian usage treats 'the Name' as a reverential shorthand for the divine/Jesus’ name; capitalization signals idiomatic status without adding words.
Given Hermas’s Roman church context where presbyters existed, 'elders' preserves potential ecclesial reference and the honor dynamic implied by seating.
Hermas contrasts simplicity with double-mindedness elsewhere; 'simplicity' keeps his ascetical-ethical category intact.

review_passes.summary: The draft is generally excellent and captures the narrative and moral tone well. However, there is a grammatical misstep in verse 6 regarding 'all your sins', and a mistranslation in verse 9 where an imperative is rendered as a future indicative and a causal conjunction is rendered as a conditional.
issues_found: In verse 6, 'πάντα' is neuter plural ('all things' or adverbial 'constantly'), not feminine plural modifying 'ἁμαρτιῶν'. The draft translates it as if it were 'πασῶν τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν' ('all your sins'). It should be 'asking all these things about your sins' or 'constantly asking about your sins'.

In verse 9, 'ὡς ἐμμένεις' uses 'ὡς' with the indicative, meaning 'as' or 'since', not 'if'. Furthermore, 'μενὸν' is an OCR error in the source text for the aorist imperative 'μεῖνον' ('remain!' or 'continue!'), not a future indicative. The text means 'But since you remain in your simplicity, continue in it, and you will sit with them'.

revisions.rationale: The double use of "for you" is awkward and repetitive. translation.text: I asked her, saying, “Lady, to what place in the field?” “Wherever you wish,” she says. I chose a good, secluded spot. But before I spoke to her and named the place, she says to me, “I will come there where you wish.”

translation.text: Seeing these things set there and no one in the place, I was astonished, and a tremor, as it were, seized me, and my hair stood on end; and a shudder, as it were, came upon me, since I was alone. Then, coming to myself and remembering the glory of God, and taking courage, I knelt and again confessed my sins to the Lord, as before.

translation.text: So when I wanted to sit on the right side, she did not permit me, but motioned to me with her hand that I should sit on the left side. So as I reasoned and was grieved that she had not allowed me to sit on the right side, she says to me, “Are you grieved, Hermas? The place on the right side belongs to others—those who have already pleased God and suffered for the sake of the Name; but you lack many things to sit with them. But as you remain in your simplicity, remain, and you will sit with them, as will all who do their works and endure what they also endured.”

translation.text: When I saw these things there and no one else around, I was amazed. It was as if trembling seized me; my hair stood on end, and it was as if a shudder came over me, because I was alone. Then I regained my composure, remembered God's glory, and took courage. I knelt down and once again confessed my sins to the Lord, as I had before.

simplification_decisions.reasoning_layer_used: POB text and independent grounding review
simplification_decisions.rationale: This natural wording avoids implying that the things were upright or animate.

simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: Both intense physical reactions remain deliberately qualified descriptions.
simplification_decisions.reasoning_layer_used: POB source-driven imagery and independent grounding review
simplification_decisions.rationale: Repeating “it was as if” preserves the narrator's hedging in clear English.

simplification_decisions.reasoning_layer_used: POB narrative sequence
simplification_decisions.rationale: The shorter clauses preserve the sequence while making it easier to follow.

spob_revision_history.previous_text: When I saw these things standing there and no one else around, I was amazed. I began to tremble, my hair stood on end, and a shiver ran through me because I was alone. Then I regained my composure and remembered God's glory. I took courage, knelt down, and once again confessed my sins to the Lord, as I had before.
spob_revision_history.review_summary: The draft is substantially clearer and preserves the narrative sequence, the reference to God's glory, and the renewed confession of sins. Revision is needed only to preserve the POB’s repeated qualified imagery (“as it were”) and to avoid adding the possible implication of uprightness in “standing there.” No doctrinally unsupported expansion is present.

base_translation.text: So when I wanted to sit on the right side, she did not permit me, but motioned to me with her hand that I should sit on the left side. So as I reasoned and was grieved that she had not allowed me to sit on the right side, she says to me, “Are you grieved, Hermas? The place on the right side belongs to others—those who have already pleased God and suffered for the sake of the Name; but you lack many things to sit with them. But as you remain in your simplicity, remain, and you will sit with them, as will all who do their works and endure what they also endured.”

translation.text:
When I tried to sit on her right, she would not let me. Instead, she motioned with her hand for me to sit on her left. I wondered why she had not let me sit on her right, and I became upset.

She said to me, “Why are you upset, Hermas? The place on the right is for others—for those who have already pleased God and suffered for the sake of the Name. You still lack much before you can sit with them. But continue to live in simplicity, as you do now, and you will sit with them. The same is true of everyone who does the works they did and endures what they endured.”

simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: Hermas reflects on the refusal and feels distressed by it.
simplification_decisions.reasoning_layer_used: POB translation and immediate narrative context
simplification_decisions.rationale: The wording expresses his thought and emotion in ordinary English.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: you lack many things to sit with them
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: You still lack much before you can sit with them
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: Hermas is not yet ready to share their honored place.
simplification_decisions.reasoning_layer_used: POB translation
simplification_decisions.rationale: This removes an unnatural construction without specifying what he lacks.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: as you remain in your simplicity, remain
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: continue to live in simplicity, as you do now
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: Hermas must persevere in his present simplicity.
simplification_decisions.reasoning_layer_used: POB translation and source-driven repetition
simplification_decisions.rationale: The command to persevere is expressed naturally while retaining the key term.

risk_flags.risk: “Simplicity” may carry a richer moral sense than the modern word suggests.
risk_flags.mitigation: The key term is retained rather than narrowed to innocence or sincerity.

risk_flags.risk: “The Name” may be unclear to readers unfamiliar with early Christian usage.
risk_flags.mitigation: The capitalized title is preserved because the record does not identify its referent more explicitly.
